A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed DSM scheme can achieve a good trade-off between the system performance, the convergence speed, and the computational complexity.
the proposed learning methods, based on imitation, are effective to achieve a stable system equilibrium with a low cost and a fast convergence speed.
, the Proportional Rule outperforms the other imitation rules in all the scenarios considered, and that it is also able to achieve a better performance than the best myopic policy.
The main takeaway from our work is that

a simple and distributed DSM policy based on imitation can achieve a good performance in terms of cost reduction and convergence rate, thus representing an appealing option for practical applications.
, by using a simple learning mechanism, the system can converge to a Nash equilibrium with low cost for both users and retailer, while avoiding the need for a centralized controller.
a fully distributed system can achieve the same results of a centralized one while being more robust and flexible.
